---
title: 'Node.js Runtime Pin'
description: 'Single-source Node.js version, where it applies, and the platforms that intentionally run a different version.'
---

The repository pins Node.js **26.12.1** in the root `.node-version` file. It is
the 2026-10-21 security release of the Node 26 Current line, which is not LTS.
Treat `.node-version` as the source of the requested version. Installing that
version and activating it are separate steps. Version managers need the setup
below; a plain `node` command can still resolve an older installation.

The workflow migration and its guard are pending in
[PR #6496](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/pull/6496). Until that layer lands,
this pin alone does not change CI runtime selection. The CI behavior and
receipts described below are the intended acceptance criteria for that layer.

The `engines.node` ranges are support floors, not runtime pins. The root
`>=22.13.0` floor stays because Vercel maps `>=22` to its newest supported
major. The `>=18.0.0` ranges in published packages are consumer contracts.
Raising either range to 26 would break Vercel deployments and package
consumers without changing the CI runtime.

## Local setup

On a personal machine, install the pinned version side by side, activate it,
and verify the version in the same shell that will run your commands.

For [fnm](https://github.com/Schniz/fnm#shell-setup), initialize the shell and
select the version explicitly:

```bash
eval "$(fnm env --use-on-cd --shell zsh)"  # use --shell bash for Bash
fnm install "$(cat .node-version)"
fnm use "$(cat .node-version)"
node --version                          # v26.12.1
```

The `--use-on-cd` hook switches to `.node-version` when entering the repository.
Installing a version without selecting it or enabling that hook is insufficient.

[mise version-file support](https://mise.jdx.dev/lang/node.html#version-files)
is opt-in. On your personal machine, enable Node version files with
`mise settings add idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools node` (this changes
mise's global configuration). With mise's shell integration active, it then
selects the repository's `.node-version`. Explicit execution works without
relying on shell activation:

```bash
mise install node@"$(cat .node-version)"
mise exec node@"$(cat .node-version)" -- node --version
```

nvm does not automatically read `.node-version`. On a personal machine, run
`nvm install "$(cat .node-version)"`, then `nvm use "$(cat .node-version)"`, and
check `node --version`; automatic directory switching requires a separate hook.

[Volta project pins](https://docs.volta.sh/guide/understanding#pinning-node-engines)
use the `volta` field in `package.json`, which this repository does not supply.
Do not assume Volta reads `.node-version`. Use an explicit one-command override,
`volta run --node "$(cat .node-version)" node --version`, or one of the managers
above instead of adding a second repository pin.

The devbox bootstrap remains distribution/LTS-based; it does not activate
`.node-version`. Select the private toolchain explicitly when validating on a
devbox, just as on other shared hosts.

### Shared agent hosts

Several projects share agent hosts, so do not use `nvm install` there. Placing
a build under `~/.nvm/versions/node` changes what nvm's major alias (for
example `26`) resolves to for every new shell, even when the alias file stays
the same. Instead:

1. Download `node-v<version>-<platform>.tar.xz`, `SHASUMS256.txt` and
   `SHASUMS256.txt.sig` from `https://nodejs.org/dist/v<version>/` into a new
   empty directory.
2. Check the SHA-256 of the tarball against `SHASUMS256.txt`. Verify the
   signature with the [Node.js release keys](https://github.com/nodejs/release-keys)
   in a temporary `GNUPGHOME`.
3. Extract the tarball to
   `~/.local/share/tuturuuu/toolchains/node-v<version>-<platform>/`.
4. Call that `bin/node` by absolute path, or prepend its `bin` to `PATH` for
   your own commands only. For queued work, use
   `ttr resources run -- <toolchain>/bin/node …`.

Do not change any of the following, which other sessions and projects share:

- nvm's aliases or `~/.nvm`;
- the `ttr resources` shims;
- Homebrew or `/usr/local` Node;
- runner tool caches;
- shared setup scripts or shell profiles.

If a change really needs one of these, stop and get the owner's approval.

`bun doctor` still enforces the Node 22 floor rather than the exact pin.

## Proving which runtime ran

A pin in `.node-version`, `engines` or `packageManager` does not prove which
Node a hosted builder or runtime used. Record four kinds of evidence
separately and do not infer one from another:

1. **Source pin**: the `.node-version` contents at the exact commit.
2. **Local artifact**: the toolchain path, the tarball SHA-256 and
   `bin/node --version`.
3. **CI**: the `setup-node` log line (`Found in cache @ …/node/<version>` or the
   download) and the job's `node --version` output, tied to the run's head SHA.
4. **Hosted and deployed runtime**: one of the following, read-only:
   - the version printed in real build logs, such as `Vercel CLI x (Node.js y)`;
   - the provider's official project setting, such as the Node.js Version from
     `vercel project inspect <project> --scope tuturuuu`.

   Record it with the project root, the install and build commands, and the
   canonical deployment identity. When none of this is observable, record
   "pin changed, hosted runtime UNVERIFIED".

As of 2026-10-23, for example:

- The `platform` Vercel project has root `apps/web` and Node.js Version `24.x`.
  It installs and builds through `apps/web/vercel.json`.
- Its last production CI build logged `Vercel CLI 59.25.0 (Node.js 24.21.0)`.
- The exact patch version of the deployed function runtime is not observable,
  because Vercel rolls patches.

## Where 26.12.1 applies after #6496

| Surface | Version | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub Actions `setup-node` steps | 26.12.1 | `node-version-file: .node-version` |
| Root script tests, SDK and package tests, Turbo tasks in CI | 26.12.1 | inherits the setup step |
| Desktop beta and store packaging jobs (Flutter desktop plus Node TypeScript scripts) | 26.12.1 | inherits the setup step |
| Dev container | 26.12.1 | `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` node feature |
| Local development | 26.12.1 | `.node-version` |

A job reads `node-version-file` only when its checkout is the workflow's own
commit (no `ref`, or `${{ github.sha }}`) and is not sparse. The file then comes
from the same tree as the workflow. Other jobs pin the literal `26.12.1`:

- jobs that set up Node before any checkout, such as package publish and dispatch;
- sparse duplicate-validation checkouts;
- jobs that check out a PR head, the `production` branch, a workflow-run head or
  an input SHA, because that tree may predate `.node-version`.

The guard proposed in #6496 (`scripts/ci/node-version-pin.test.js`) requires every literal to equal
`.node-version` and every exception to be listed. The shared planner in
`scripts/ci/node-version-pin.js` regenerates workflow inputs and validation path
filters with `node scripts/ci/node-version-pin.js --write`. It requires a real
Vercel invocation in that job of a `vercel-*` workflow before granting the
Node 24.22.1 exception. A foreign, sparse or differently conditioned checkout
cannot supply the version file. Pin-only changes must pass both workflow event
filters and the shared Cloudflare affected-path selector;
`scripts/ci/node-version-selection.test.js` exercises Colab, Cron Control and
Lettin with an unrelated-path negative control. The guard also requires each
`test "$(node --version)" = v…` workflow assertion to name the pin.

Each setup step logs the resolved version. Two receipts bind `node --version` to
the exact source SHA:

- the SDK qualification receipt (`runtimeVersions.node` with `sourceSha`);
- the Calendar native artifact receipt (`node` with `sha`).

## Intentional exceptions

| Surface | Runs | Why | Patched fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `employee-schema-contract.yaml` | Node 24.22.1 | It qualifies an input source SHA whose chat qualification binds a Node 24 runtime identity (`chat-initial-settings-qualification.mjs`). | 24.22.1 is the latest patched 24.x (2026-10-20 security release). |
| `supabase-staging.yaml` | Node 24 (floating patch) | `supabase-production.yaml` admits staging completions only from allowlisted git blob SHAs of this file. #6496 preserves its bytes; any later setup-step change needs a coordinated gate update. | A floating `24` can use a cached patch; pinning 24.22.1 or adding `check-latest: true` needs that coordinated update. |
| Vercel Functions and the `vercel build` / `vercel deploy` workflows | Node 24.x | [Vercel supports only 24.x (default) and 22.x](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js/node-js-versions). The CI build should match the function runtime it produces. | `node-version: 24.22.1` fixes the CI patch; Vercel applies patches to the function runtime independently. |
| Cloudflare Workers | workerd, not Node | Workers implement Node APIs through the `nodejs_compat` flag and `compatibility_date`. That date is set in each `wrangler.jsonc`; the Node version is not configurable. | Advance `compatibility_date` deliberately with each Worker's acceptance tests. |
| Supabase Edge Functions | Deno | The repository ships no Edge Functions today. Supabase Edge would run Deno, not Node. | Not applicable. |
| JavaScript actions (`runs.using`) | Runner-embedded Node 24 | [Action metadata accepts only `node20` and `node24`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/metadata-syntax). `setup-node` does not change it. | GitHub maintains the runner-embedded runtime. |
| Local docs (`bun dev:docs`, docs validation) | Node 24.19.0 through `npx` | Mintlify CLI 4.2.520 rejects Node 25+, and its Got 12.6.1 connectivity probe crashes on Node 24.20+ (see [Mintlify runtime compatibility](/build/development-tools/documenting#mintlify-runtime-compatibility)). The host can run 26.12.1; the wrapper launches an isolated Node 24.19.0. | Upgrade Mintlify to a CLI that accepts Node 26 and reassess the Got defect, then move the pin. |
| Docker images (`apps/web`, `apps/hive`, `apps/docs`, `apps/web/docker/native-runner.Dockerfile`) | `node:24-bookworm-slim` | The Docker runtime is paused (see [active runtime policy](/build/devops/active-runtime)), and `scripts/check-docker-web.js` enforces the retained builder stage. | On resumption, use `node:26.12.1-bookworm-slim`, digest `sha256:28147155d47dc31abe0a46e0d12b59b2fb3d0a2dcc5dc65fce76a074180b16fe` as of 2026-10-21. |
| `apps/tanstack-web`, `apps/backend`, and workflows disabled in `tuturuuu.ci.ts` | Unchanged | These runtimes are paused; their retained source and workflows are not updated. | Not applicable. |
| Flutter (`apps/mobile`) | Flutter/Dart SDK | Flutter tooling does not use Node. Only the Node scripts around it follow the pin. | Not applicable. |
| Electron | Not used | No workspace depends on Electron; desktop builds use Flutter. | Not applicable. |
| `.idx/dev.nix` | `nodejs_20` | This Firebase Studio template depends on the nixpkgs channel that template pins. | Update it when that channel ships a Node 26 attribute. |

A floating `node-version: 24` does not guarantee the newest patch:
[setup-node defaults `check-latest` to false](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/blob/main/docs/advanced-usage.md#check-latest-version)
and first accepts a matching cached release. An exact patched version gives a
reproducible CI selection; `check-latest: true` instead requests the newest
matching release. Neither proves which patch a deployed function runs.

## Native addons

Node 26 uses `NODE_MODULE_VERSION` 147 and N-API 10. sharp, bcrypt,
better-sqlite3, esbuild, lightningcss, `@swc/core`, `@napi-rs/canvas`,
`@napi-rs/keyring` and `node:sqlite` all load and run on 26.12.1.
better-sqlite3 is the only one tied to a V8 ABI, so reinstall it after a major
Node change.

## Updating the pin

1. Read the target from `https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json`, including its
   `security` and `lts` fields.
2. Change `.node-version`, plus any pre-checkout `node-version` literals the
   workflow contract tests list.
3. Run the root script tests and the affected package tests with that exact
   binary through `ttr resources run`.
4. Check the CI setup logs and the SDK qualification receipt for the new
   `node --version` on the exact commit.
5. Re-check every exception above against its upstream documentation.
